description.content:
Issue usage-based charges to customers

We highly recommend using the PUT method to prevent creation of duplicate usage records

The POST method creates new usage records and allows creation of duplicates. For example: if you submit a usage record with start_time 12:15 UTC and 12:30 UTC for the same customer, product and dimension, two usage records will be created for that hour. We do not aggregate the submitted quantities. Be aware that marketplaces don't allow the submission of duplicates by default, it's usually only allowed for special reconciliation scenarios.

Customers can be identified in two different ways: by either providing `customer_id` and `product_id`, or by providing `subscription_id`

If a usage record doesn't already exist for the submitted customer, product, dimension and start_time hour, a new record will be created. If there is an existing record, the quantity will be updated if the record hasn't already been submitted to the marketplace. However, if the record has already been submitted to the marketplace, a 409 - Conflict error will be returned

info.name: Tackle Public Contracts Authentication Metering API

description.content:
Customer-facing read API for cloud marketplace contracts that Tackle has
ingested for your Tackle account.

The response shape is a stable projection of the underlying
contract document. It is intended to be safe to consume long-term: fields
will be added over time, but documented fields will not be removed without
deprecation notice.

## Authentication

Every request must include a valid Tackle JWT in the `Authorization`
header (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`). Machine-to-machine (MTM) tokens
issued for your Tackle account are accepted. The token scopes every
response to the account it represents.

## Pagination

`GET /api/contracts` is the only paginated endpoint. Pagination uses an
opaque `cursor` query parameter:

1. The first request omits `cursor`.
2. If more pages exist, the response includes a `next` field. Pass that
   value verbatim back as `cursor` on the next request.
3. The last page omits `next`.

Cursors are opaque tokens. Do not parse, modify, or persist them across
schema changes — request a fresh page from the start instead.
